terms.definition: An electron in the outermost shell of an atom.
terms.function: The electron shared or transferred when atoms bond.
terms.whereItIs: The single bright dot on sodium's outer ring in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Valence electrons control how atoms bond and how reactive they are.

terms.definition: The outermost electron shell of an atom.
terms.function: Holds the valence electrons — the layer where bonding happens.
terms.whereItIs: The outer ring of the sodium atom.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the shell that interacts with other atoms.

terms.definition: An electron in a shell closer to the nucleus than the valence shell.
terms.function: Fills the inner shells but does not participate in bonding.
terms.whereItIs: The small dim dots on sodium's inner ring.
terms.whyItMatters: Contrasting them with valence electrons clarifies which electrons actually bond.

terms.definition: A column of the periodic table whose elements share the same number of valence electrons.
terms.function: Explains why elements in a column behave alike.
terms.whereItIs: Sodium's column (group 1) — every element in it has one valence electron.
terms.whyItMatters: The group-valence link is the heart of periodic table patterns.
